revelation.work: Plays of Sophocles: Oedipus the King, Oedipus at Colonus, Antigone
revelation.author: Sophocles
revelation.locator: Oedipus the King, the herdsman confirms the foundling; local text, normalized characters 52812-53512
revelation.excerpt: Friend, he that stands before thee was that child. HERDSMAN. A plague upon thee! Hold thy wanton tongue! OEDIPUS. Softly, old man, rebuke him not; thy words Are more deserving chastisement than his. HERDSMAN. O best of masters, what is my offense? OEDIPUS. Not answering what he asks about the child. HERDSMAN. He speaks at random, babbles like a fool. OEDIPUS. If thou lack’st grace to speak, I’ll loose thy tongue. HERDSMAN. For mercy’s sake abuse not an old man. OEDIPUS. Arrest the villain, seize and pinion him! HERDSMAN. Alack, alack! What have I done? what wouldst thou further learn? OEDIPUS. Didst give this man the child of whom he asks? HERDSMAN. I did; and would that I had died that day!

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: To free Thebes from plague, Oedipus seeks Laius’ killer and curses the unknown culprit. The investigation eventually identifies Oedipus himself. The skill and determination used to protect the city turn back upon its ruler.

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: The messenger connects Oedipus with the infant given away by Laius' household; the herdsman confirms he passed the child on.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Watch how the proclamation changes meaning as the inquiry proceeds. Oedipus speaks against an unknown culprit, while the audience can recognise that his investigation will expose the speaker himself.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: This is heroic problem-solving turned into reversal.
